resources.string: Turns on the Palette and Parameters filter panel and the Original colour style in the Xiaomi Camera, with the Leica Essential mode in the standard UI and an optional CMOS (M10R) style.
Leica Essential Mode in Standard UI
Show Leica Essential mode (M3/M9) in the standard UI mode strip. Real M3/M9 processing needs the 17 Ultra/18 Pro Max HAL; on other devices enable the compatibility fallback below.
Enable the Leica Looks panel in the filter strip. When off, uses the standard filter UI.
Add the CMOS (M10R) style to the photography styles picker. Requires Leica UI enabled.

Show Original in the Portrait style picker. On by default on the 17 Ultra and 18 Pro Max; off by default on the 14 Ultra, whose camera hardware layer cannot complete the Original portrait preview session — enabling it there may freeze the preview. Original colour in Photo mode is not affected. Restart Camera after changing this.
When the Legendary HAL plugin is missing, forward M9/M3 to the stock Leica Authentic/Vibrant colour path. This is an approximation, not the real M3/M9 processing. Off by default.
Enable extra film simulation filters: R600, P100F, F-50, KC64, KP160.
Render M3/M9 in the camera engine (HAL LUT slot)

Hand the look to the stock filter node instead of post-processing the photo. Requires the LUT file installed in /data/vendor/camera (tools/hal-port/engine/leica_look.sh) and the Negative filter selected. Restart Camera and the camera provider after changing this or the LUT.
M3 and M9 as their own Looks entries

Add M3 and M9 chips to the Leica Looks panel. They render the module LUTs (lut_m3.png / lut_m9.png in /data/vendor/camera) through the stock filter node; every stock filter and look stays untouched. Install the two files with tools/hal-port/engine/leica_look.sh look-m3 / look-m9, then restart Camera.
Hide the HyperCameraMod icon from the app drawer. You can still access settings from Vector/LSPosed module list.
